newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Guatemala, China said agreed on U.N. peacekeepers.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala, China said agreed on U.N. peacekeepers.

text.p: China and Guatemala have reached an understanding that will enable the Security Council to approve sending U.N. military observers to Guatemala to monitor an accord ending the civil war there, diplomats said on Monday.
The council was expected to approve the peacekeeping mission later in the day, they added.
On Jan. 10 China exercised its veto for the first time in nearly 25 years to kill a resolution supported by all 14 other council members to send 155 military observers to Guatemala.
Beijing did not object to the peacekeeping mission itself but was reacting to Guatemala's diplomatic and other ties with Taiwan, regarded by China as a renegade province.
Intensive negotiations over the past 10 days have resulted in an understanding that now enables China to lift its opposition, the sources said.

One element was said to be an undertaking by Guatemala to refrain in future from co-sponsoring an annual General Assembly resolution aimed at securing U.N. membership for Taiwan, which was expelled from the world body in 1971 and replaced by Beijing as the rightful representative of China.
